title: AI Fashion Lookbook Photos and Outfit Ads | AIVideosUGC
description: Turn one outfit photo into photos of the full outfit worn together. Use them on a collection page or a launch ad, and check each piece you can ship.
h1: AI Lookbook Photos for One Complete Outfit
lead: Get a clothing ad from a coat and scarf worn as one set. You bring the picture where both pieces show. You do not start from a blank page.
steps_h2: Make Outfit Photos for the Collection in 3 Steps
steps_lead: Leave with a still and a clip of the set: open the frame, add the jacket, the tee, and the trouser, and download.

steps.d: Pick the frame keeping the jacket with the trouser as one worn set. The set is ready without booking a model.
Upload one photo where every piece in the set is visible, or paste the collection link. Change the spoken line so it names the set.
Take a still for the collection page and a captioned clip worn by an AI avatar. Check the jacket hem against the shippable piece.

faq.q: What do I get from a lookbook template?
faq.a: A frame that holds a cardigan, a tank, and a skirt together as one worn set. Add that photo. An AI avatar wears the three pieces. You do not have to book a model.

faq.q: How do I go from the template to a look video?
faq.a: Put in the photo that shows every piece you actually ship in the set. Write a line that names the set.

faq.q: Which clothes belong in a look?
faq.a: Pieces you sell as a combination a person can put on, whether that is a rain set or a dinner set. If one piece in the photo is not for sale, leave it out of the frame.

faq.q: Can one collection become more than one look?
faq.a: Yes. Keep the blazer and swap the shirt color for the next render. A long rail of sizes can share the blazer photo.

faq.q: Who should build looks this way?
faq.a: A clothing shop that posts sets rather than single tees, and does not keep a model on a retainer. The person who writes the caption can build the look.

faq.q: What if I have never made a clothing video?
faq.a: You can still make the look. Start from the outfit photo and one sentence, even if you have never edited a video.

faq.q: When do I have a look file I can post?
faq.a: After the render. You can post in that same sitting, and you do not need to book a studio.

faq.q: What does a look photo or a clip cost?
faq.a: A still spends 24 credits. A clip spends 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, and 120 for 30. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. A failed job returns its credits. The file has no watermark.

faq.q: Where can I use the look, including a launch?
faq.a: On a collection page, in a swipeable set, or in a launch email after you add prices yourself. A launch that also needs video is covered by [product launch video and photos](page:occ-product-launch).

faq.q: What should I compare before I post?
faq.a: Check each piece you can actually ship: color, outline, and what is included. The person on screen is an AI avatar.

steps.prompt: An adult wears the ivory tailored suit and faces the camera. The jacket, trousers, shoes, and bag stay visible. Bright daylight keeps the full outfit easy to see.

reviews.lead: Examples of how a shop builds the set, including menswear and a collection launch. Check each piece against what you can ship.

items.t: One finished frame from the outfit photo
items.d: Example: a shop uploads the full outfit and gets one photo for the collection page. If a piece is missing, it stays out of the picture.

items.t: The still and a short clip together
items.d: Example: the shop makes the still photo and a short outfit clip from the same photo, in one project.

items.t: Menswear lookbook photos from a link
items.d: Example: a menswear shop pastes the product page link, or uploads the suit, and keeps jacket, trousers, and shoes in one frame.

items.t: An AI actor, then a trim in the editor
items.d: Example: the shop picks an AI actor, a generated person, for the main outfit. It then trims the short clip and adds words on screen.

items.t: The same look in another language
items.d: Example: the swipeable row keeps one framing and one light. The spoken line on the clip is recorded again for a second market.

items.t: Music and a voiceover on the clip
items.d: Example: the outfit photo stays a still. On the video, the editor adds a spoken voice and a track from the music library.

items.t: An AI actor instead of a fitting day
items.d: Example: a boutique uses an AI actor for the main outfit. Someone new to photos can start from one flat lay, a top-down photo.

items.t: The same person across the launch
items.d: Example: a digital twin, the same generated person, wears each look so the set feels connected. Each outfit still has its own source photo.

items.t: A script, then a second framing
items.d: Example: the agency pastes the product link, takes a short script, and makes a second framing from the same outfit photo.

items.t: Publish the clip, or start from the API
items.d: Example: after the lengths match what you can ship, the shop posts the clip to Instagram or TikTok. The API lets the product list start the next outfit.

more_sections.h2: What a Lookbook Template Can Carry
more_sections.lead: The clip can carry a voice, captions, and music, and the still can sit on the collection page.

items.d: A voice can read the line, captions can name the set, and a track can come from the music library. The lookbook frame can stay a still.

items.t: AI Avatars and an AI Twin
items.d: An AI avatar wears the outfit. An AI twin can repeat that same presenter across the collection.

items.t: A Script From a Line or a Link
items.d: A short script, or a product link, can start from that page's outfit photo.
One outfit photo can make another crop for the next slide. Each photo is 24 credits, shown first.
You can trim in the editor, then send it to TikTok, Instagram, or Facebook. The file has no watermark.
The line can go out in another language, or the API can start the next outfit from your catalog.
